results.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin: Overview, architecture, performance, and uses - CUDO Compute
results.author: Emmanuel Ohiri
highlights:
NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 combines 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs in a single NVLink domain, and it is the flagship compute rack of the Vera Rubin platform, succeeding Grace Blackwell. NVIDIA announced it at CES in January 2026 and has said that production shipments begin this fall.

Those chips are distributed across five rack-scale systems rather than assembled into one cabinet, and the systems combine into ... A full POD runs to 40 racks, holding 1,152 Rubin GPUs, close to 20,000 dies and 1.2 quadrillion transistors, and NVIDIA rates it at 60 exaflops with 10 PB/s of scale-up bandwidth.

...

* These figures have been superseded since the 2025 announcement. Per-GPU HBM4 bandwidth was originally given as 13 TB/s and is now 22 TB/s, and NVLink 6 was quoted at 250 TB/s before settling at 260. The rack headline numbers moved from 3.5 exaflops of NVFP4 and 1.4 PB/s of memory bandwidth to 3,600 PFLOPS and 1,580 TB/s. The 75 TB of fast memory quoted for the rack was an aggregate of HBM and LPDDR, and reconciles with the current 20.7 TB of HBM4 plus up to 54 TB of LPDDR5X. CPU memory is the maximum installable rather than the amount shipped.

...

NVIDIA puts Vera Rubin NVL72 at one-tenth the cost per million tokens and up to ten times the tokens per megawatt of GB200 NVL72, running Kimi-K2-Thinking at a 32K input and 8K output length. Training a 10T mixture-of-experts model on 100T tokens within a fixed one-month window takes a quarter as many GPUs on Vera Rubin NVL72 as on GB200 NVL72.

...

NVIDIA’s own figures, first shown at Hot Chips 2026 and updated in September with data from the agentic benchmark below, put Vera Rubin NVL72 at up to 30 times the throughput per megawatt of GB300 NVL72, rising from about ten times as the interactivity target climbs, and at 45 times lower token cost. The Hot Chips presentation also gave a 13 percent reduction in peak power for LLM training on NVL72, and 40 percent more GPUs per provisioned watt as a system-level figure.

The first third-party verified results, published in September 2026 on early pre-release TensorRT-LLM software, ran DeepSeek V4 Pro at FP4 on a production Rubin rack. Against the strongest GB300 NVL72 configuration at each interactivity target, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered about 1.45 times the throughput per megawatt at 75 tokens per second per user, 2.1 times at 100, and 7.2 times at 150, narrowing to 2.7 times at 200. ... The results are published as a preview, subject to change as validation continues.
